credit_ratings.summary: S&P raised AMC's issuer credit rating to B- from CCC+, with a stable outlook. The reasons given were better operating performance, lower debt (much of it reduced through equity issuance and debt-to-equity conversions) and a path to sustained positive free cash flow. S&P's estimates were about $3.8B of debt, more than $450M of annual interest and about $850M of yearly rent, with a modest free-cash-flow deficit in 2026 and about $75M positive in 2027. The date is the article's publication date; the article does not give the date of S&P's action.

Moody's raised AMC's Corporate Family Rating to B3 from Caa2. It rated the new first-lien term loan B and first-lien notes due 2031 at B1, changed the outlook to positive from stable, and raised the speculative-grade liquidity rating to SGL-3 from SGL-4. The action was tied to the refinancing plan.

In the Q3 release, the CEO said the major credit rating agencies had 'meaningfully upgraded our credit rating.' A Fitch action (reported as IDR B- affirmed with a positive outlook) could not be verified from a page I opened.

debt_events.summary: AMC fully redeemed $125.5M of its 6.125% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027.

AMC completed a refinancing of about $3.97B, roughly 97% of its debt. The new debt is $2.0B of 8.875% first-lien notes due October 2031, an $850M first-lien term loan at SOFR+450bp due October 2031, and a $1.12B second-lien term loan at 11.25% due October 2033. The proceeds paid off the 7.500% senior secured notes due 2029, redeemed Muvico's 2029 senior secured notes and repaid the AMC and Odeon Finco term loans. This was a market refinancing, not a distressed exchange, and it removes the 2029 maturity wall. The 11.25% second-lien loan keeps the cost of debt high.

Management says about $2B of debt and deferred theatre rent has been repaid since 2020 and that it will keep paying down debt. It also said it will keep using equity financings 'when it makes sense,' so further shareholder dilution is possible.

distress_signals.summary: Fleet shrinkage: 3 theatres closed in Q3 2026. Since 2020, 228 locations have closed and 66 opened, a net reduction of about 162 (around 16% of the circuit). About 85 leases come up for renewal each year, and underperforming sites may close if the lease can't be renegotiated. AMC is also cutting European overhead (more than $10M of potential savings). No layoffs were announced. The CEO (Adam Aron) and CFO (Sean Goodman) are unchanged.

No going-concern language. The 10-Q says cash will be 'sufficient to fund its operations and satisfy its obligations currently and through the next twelve months,' and that operating cash flow was positive for the nine months.
Q2 2026 showed a net loss of $11.4M despite record revenue. Debt reduction has relied heavily on dilutive equity (892.6M Class A shares outstanding at 2026-07-22).

ownership.value: Publicly listed (NYSE: AMC) and widely held, with no controlling sponsor. No change of control was found.

output.risk_rationale: AMC's credit has improved sharply. S&P raised it to B- (July 2026), Moody's to B3 with a positive outlook and SGL-3 liquidity (September 2026), and the October 5, 2026 refinancing of $3.97B pushed about 97% of debt out to 2031/2033. Q3 2026 brought record revenue of $1.71B, adjusted EBITDA of $347.5M, positive free cash flow, $751.9M of cash and no going-concern language. Risk is still elevated because both ratings remain deep in speculative grade and the debt load is large: about $3.78B principal of borrowings plus $3.76B of operating lease liabilities, more than $450M of annual interest (S&P estimate) and an 11.25% second-lien loan. The business depends on the box office, keeps closing theatres and has repeatedly relied on dilutive equity to deleverage.
